sources.title: Bolivia: Rural Community Flood and Drought Resilience in the Bolivian Highlands
sources.temporal_coverage: EVAs project implementation in 2011–2017; terminal evaluation in 2017; post-completion assessment in 2023; regional climate modeling through 2070.
sources.methodology: Five-page case study synthesizes project-close and 2023 post-completion evaluations.
sources.limitations: Regional evaluation synthesis, not a representative climate-impact survey.

sources.title: Impacts of Wildfires on Economic, Social, Cultural and Environmental Rights and Biodiversity: Report of REDESCA's Working Visit to Bolivia
sources.organization: Inter-American Commission on Human Rights, Office of the Special Rapporteur on Economic, Social, Cultural and Environmental Rights (REDESCA)
sources.temporal_coverage: Examines the 2024 wildfire emergency; REDESCA mission conducted 9–11 December 2024; report approved 30 May 2025.
sources.methodology: Mission to La Paz, Santa Cruz and San Ignacio; reviewed official information and community testimony.
sources.limitations: Field mission, not a representative survey or fire-attribution study.

sources.title: De la emergencia a la gestión de riesgos por sequía: el caso de las ciudades de La Paz y El Alto en Bolivia y sus lecciones aprendidas
sources.organization: Inter-American Development Bank, Water and Sanitation Division
sources.temporal_coverage: Reviews the 2016–2017 and 2022–2023 drought episodes, the EPSAS drought-management protocol introduced in 2018, and system operation through 2024.
sources.methodology: Full 114-page Spanish note using EPSAS operational data.
sources.limitations: Provider case study; household impacts unmeasured.

sources.title: Adaptation Planning in Bolivia
sources.organization: United Nations Development Programme Accelerator Lab Bolivia
sources.temporal_coverage: Reports on a UNDP Accelerator Lab adaptation-planning prototype; page does not state implementation dates.
sources.methodology: Read the full case study describing deliberative workshops, a community survey and co-designed planning map.
sources.limitations: The case is explicitly a prototype/pilot, not an evaluation of institutionalized or scaled adaptation outcomes.

sources.title: Bolivia, Country Strategic Outcome 2: Decentralized Evaluation (2023–2025)
sources.organization: World Food Programme, Office of Evaluation
sources.temporal_coverage: Evaluation covers WFP Bolivia Country Strategic Plan outcome implementation from January 2023 through December 2024.
sources.methodology: Read the complete official evaluation synopsis page; its linked evaluation PDF required JavaScript bot verification and was not read.
sources.limitations: Claims are limited to the posted synopsis; detailed evaluation methods and findings were not verified in the PDF.

claims.locator: One-based PDF pp. 1–2, climate context and regional modeling
claims.paraphrase: In southeastern Oruro and northern Potosí, models project drier dry seasons and wetter wet seasons with more floods and droughts; Quechua and Aymara highland farmers rely on rainfed or small-irrigation systems.
claims.scenario: Regional modeling gives 7–20% higher annual precipitation and 0.9–3.3°C warming by 2070; emissions pathway unspecified.

claims.locator: One-based PDF p. 2, 2023 drought and livelihood impacts
claims.paraphrase: The report attributes the 2023 highland drought to climate-related heat and El Niño: water flows fell one-third, and crop losses affected nearly two million farmers across seven departments including Oruro and Potosí.
claims.limitations: The nearly two-million farmer estimate spans seven departments, not only project ayllus.

claims.locator: One-based PDF pp. 3–4, project results and 2023 post-completion visits
claims.paraphrase: By 2023, visited irrigation systems remained operational under local maintenance; participating farmers continued selling crops during drought while neighboring rainfed communities struggled.
geographies: 12 ayllus in southeastern Oruro and northern Potosí
claims.limitations: Post-completion visits, not representative impact estimates.

claims.locator: One-based PDF p. 3, land-use planning results and continuity
claims.paraphrase: Only two of six municipalities ratified project land-use plans, and turnover weakened their use; ayllu bylaws remained active for land management and resolving disputes with neighboring communities.
claims.limitations: Local dispute resolution is not evidence of violence.

claims.locator: Printed pp. 10–11, paragraphs 15–24, affected regions and Indigenous territories
claims.paraphrase: Over 2.5 million hectares burned in lowland Indigenous territories; Chiquitanía fires consumed 92% of forest in Guarayo, Monte Verde and Pantanal territories.

claims.locator: Printed p. 35, paragraphs 118–122, access to water
claims.paraphrase: San Ignacio de Velasco Chiquitano communities faced fire-worsened water scarcity, reduced flows from private dams, agrochemical contamination and reportedly unenforced drought rules.
institutions: San Ignacio de Velasco municipal government

claims.locator: Printed p. 44, paragraph 162, Ayoreo people in voluntary isolation
claims.paraphrase: 2024 fires threatened Ayoreo in Chaco dry forests; damage to isolated Ayoreo territory was unknown.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Fire-damaged habitat could force unwanted Ayoreo contact, exposing them to disease and violence.

claims.locator: Printed pp. 16–17 and 44, paragraphs 46–50 and 165, fire-season land conflicts
claims.paraphrase: Fire-season reports described pressure, invasion and disputes over Indigenous lands in Santa Cruz.
claims.limitations: Not armed violence or climate attribution.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: REDESCA says groups exploited fire-disaster chaos to contest collective lands, worsening pre-existing tenure tensions.

claims.locator: Printed pp. 29–30, La Paz and El Alto drought impacts in 2016–2017
claims.paraphrase: In 2016–2017, rainfall deficits reached 36% in La Paz–El Alto; 256,000 people in 100 La Paz neighborhoods and seven El Alto districts faced water rationing.

claims.locator: Printed pp. 54–57, comparison of 2016–2017 and 2022–2023 drought outcomes
claims.paraphrase: The 2022–2023 drought was meteorologically longer and more intense than 2016–2017, yet EPSAS reported no service restrictions or cuts after its drought protocol and system measures.
claims.limitations: EPSAS service outcome, not household welfare.

claims.paraphrase: The IDB note presents an illustrative pathway from drought emergency management to social and political conflict.
claims.scenario: Conditional hypothetical; no Bolivian event or probability is reported.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Opaque, improvised restrictions may undermine trust and trigger social conflict, possibly escalating politically.

claims.locator: Printed p. 27, national and subnational drought plans
claims.paraphrase: No implemented national drought plan existed; a 2023–2024 response allocated over BOB 187 million to 156 municipalities.
systems: Plurinational Immediate Response Plan to Drought

claims.locator: Case study, problem statement and climate-action gaps
claims.paraphrase: UNDP identifies underrepresentation of Indigenous views in Lifesystems plans and no established pathway to integrate hyperlocal priorities into municipal PTDIs and national adaptation planning.
claims.limitations: The case study describes a pilot planning process, not nationwide representation.

claims.locator: Case study, Kaami adaptation prototype and participation results
claims.paraphrase: Camiri allocated a budget to connect Kaami's plan with municipal planning; workshops engaged 16 of 19 Chaco Indigenous communities and produced a co-designed 3D map for the municipal planning process.
claims.limitations: UNDP labels the experience a prototype/pilot; institutional uptake is not verified.

claims.locator: Official evaluation synopsis, context and intervention description
claims.paraphrase: WFP's Oruro intervention addressed rural poverty and water scarcity affecting climate-vulnerable smallholder subsistence producers and Indigenous communities through cash transfers and water-related productive assets.
claims.limitations: Evaluation synopsis only; detailed geographic coverage is not provided on the page.

claims.locator: Official evaluation synopsis, overall findings and recommendations
claims.paraphrase: WFP's synopsis says cash transfers protected consumption after climate shocks, while their contribution to longer-term resilience remained unclear; it describes Urus water-access results as significant but needing better tailoring.
claims.limitations: The evaluation page recommends stronger maintenance partnerships; linked full evaluation PDF was inaccessible.

search_audit.query: Bolivia named subnational climate vulnerability Oruro Potosí La Paz El Alto drought wildfire Indigenous rural communities primary reports
search_audit.outcome: Read the World Bank highlands case, REDESCA fire report, IDB La Paz–El Alto drought note and WFP Oruro evaluation synopsis for named local exposure and group differentiation.

search_audit.query: Bolivia climate drought wildfire displacement violence land tenure Indigenous conflict mediators primary sources
search_audit.outcome: REDESCA reports fire-emergency land disputes and a conditional Ayoreo forced-contact/violence risk; the IDB note describes a generic drought-governance-to-social-conflict pathway, not a documented climate-caused violent event.

search_audit.query: Bolivia conflict violence insecurity disrupted climate adaptation irrigation water systems early warning reverse pathway official evaluation
search_audit.outcome: No reviewed source establishes organized violence interrupting adaptation delivery. REDESCA reports land-related social conflict in the fire emergency; the World Bank notes political turnover weakened plan continuity, not conflict-related disruption.

search_audit.query: Bolivia Oruro Potosí La Paz resilience capacity irrigation early warning drought plans Indigenous adaptation municipal planning evaluation
search_audit.outcome: Reviewed irrigation maintenance and ayllu governance, EPSAS drought protocol and service outcomes, the Camiri–Kaami planning pilot, and WFP water-access/cash-transfer evaluation findings; broader scale-up remains limited or unverified.

gaps: No reviewed primary source establishes armed conflict or organized violence disrupting climate-adaptation delivery in Bolivia; documented social conflict and land disputes are localized and not evidence of climate-caused violence.

REDESCA's 2024 wildfire mission is not representative and does not establish climate-change attribution for ignition; its Ayoreo forced-contact pathway is a conditional risk, not an observed violence event.

The full WFP evaluation PDF required JavaScript bot verification, and the FAO 2025 Oruro–Potosí anticipatory-action PDF exceeded the reader's size limit; claims rely only on accessible official page text or other opened reports.

The UNDP 2021 Oruro resilience report PDF returned 403; no claim relies on its body. The World Bank EVAs findings are based on project evaluations and 2023 site visits, with limited replication and municipal-plan continuity.
